chapter: Hollywood life and the musicians' union
title: Settling down in Hollywood and giving up the band
summary: Tired of never getting a hit record, Carter chose a settled life writing for films.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Well, we've come to a kind of period in the late 40's, you are working to some extent, in Hollywood in a variety of kinds of work; you don't have a regular band any more, but you put bands together every now and then, and take dates ... you are composing, recording, working in Hollywood; do you see this ...
Well, I'm not really composing yet. I'm writing songs.
No, you're writing songs. I know that. I meant that you were still writing music.
Right. And some beautiful tunes, you know. The records that you're making ... and then later

you do some special records with Count Basie and others and so on, for which you were composing a great deal. Also, your "Jazz Calendar, you made about half the tunes or so on that 12, monthly idols, if you can call them that.

Do you ... this of course, must have appeared to you as a very different mode of life from the one that you had led with your occasional bands in Europe, on the road and so on. Did that begin to give you more satisfaction in a personal way to lead a more ... or a less geographically mobile existence?

I guess so. I kind of felt a little like settling down and taking it a little easier, and I was becoming more interested, you know, as I went along in writing for films, as we had said before. And I wasn't satisfied with, you know, the sweet smell of failure, as I mentioned before -- but I was experiencing with the band -- we weren't really making a lot of money. Just doing all right, you know? But for all the work that was going in to it, it looked like we were never gonna get a hit record, and a hit record was really the thing that would really catapult you in to the Big Time, you know -- it was what you really needed.
And I just thought I'd stop fighting it.

Right. But did that give you some leisure to pursue other interests? You know, I know that you ... is that when you became interested in art and read more, I mean, when you had a more settled kind of existence?
I guess so. Yes, I got a little lazier.
